headline: Brain-response models are audited and trained against standardized data and benchmarks
label: Brain Model Evaluation Foundations
summary: Three preprints show brain models judged against sensory maps, pooled pretraining data, and challenge benchmarks, so evaluation design shapes conclusions.
synthesis: The current items do not share the earlier multiverse-reanalysis and EEG rich-club evidence, so that thread is not retained. The common thread is how neuroimaging models are assessed and what data they rest on. The TRIBE v2 audit tests a multimodal fMRI response model against classic sensory maps, finding no retinotopy or tonotopy but strong MT+ motion selectivity. Open-fMIND supplies a uniformly preprocessed corpus (322 OpenNeuro studies, 11,379 subjects, 2.4M timeseries) for self-supervised pretraining of brain foundation models. The BraTS-PEDs study applies a multi-stage nnU-Net with a rare-aware residual adapter to pediatric tumor subregion segmentation under challenge conditions. What is new is the pairing of explicit biological validation with standardized corpora and benchmarks. All three are preprints, so results remain preliminary.
